docs.title: UmbraScript
docs.text:
UmbraScript is an xTalk-style scripting language for inspecting and automating content and media in Umbraco CMS.

UmbraScript
show content at "/destinations/pensacola-florida/"

Use readable statements to find content, update properties, publish a branch, or organize media without writing a one-off application.

Install UmbraScript Run your first command

docs.title: Work with content
docs.text:
Inspect, create, publish, unpublish, rename, move, copy, trash, and restore content nodes.

Browse content commands

docs.title: Work with properties
docs.text:
Read property values across a selection, then set or clear values when you need to make a controlled change.

Browse property commands

docs.title: Work with media
docs.text:
Inspect the media tree, create folders, and rename, move, copy, trash, or restore media items.

Browse media commands

docs.title: Designed for Umbraco
docs.text:
UmbraScript uses familiar Umbraco concepts: content keys, content routes, Document Type aliases, property aliases, the content tree, and the media tree. Keywords are case-insensitive, while names, paths, aliases, and values are written as quoted strings.

UmbraScript is free to use with Umbraco CMS 17 and later.

Support UmbraScript

New to UmbraScript?

Start with the five-minute first-command tutorial. It uses a read-only command and explains the result before introducing commands that change your site.

docs.title: UmbraScript
docs.text:
UmbraScript is a talk-like scripting language for inspecting and automating content and media in Umbraco CMS.

Use readable statements in a dedicated backoffice section to inspect a tree, update properties, publish a branch, or organize media without building a one-off application.

docs.title: What you can do
docs.text:
• Inspect, create, publish, unpublish, rename, move, copy, trash, and restore content.
  • Read, set, and clear content property values by alias.
  • Inspect and organize media, including creating folders and moving items.
  • Target one item by key or path, its direct children, or all of its descendants.
  • Review structured JSON results with per-item outcomes for batch operations.

UmbraScript uses familiar Umbraco concepts such as content routes, content keys, Document Type aliases, property aliases, and the content and media trees. Keywords are case-insensitive, while names, paths, aliases, and values are written as quoted strings.

docs.title: See it in action
docs.text:
Inspect one content item without changing it:

show content at "/destinations/pensacola-florida/"

Inspect every descendant below a branch:

show content below "/news/"

Update a property on the direct children of an item:

set property "region" of content in "/destinations/" to "Midwest"

Publish every descendant below a branch:

publish content below "/news/"

Move a media item into another folder:

move media at "/Images/legacy-logo.png" to at "/Images/Archive/"

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
UmbraScript is free to use with Umbraco CMS 17 and later.

Add the package to the directory containing your Umbraco project:

dotnet add package UmbraScript

Build and restart the website. Then, as an administrator, open Users, select the appropriate user group, and enable the UmbraScript section under Assign access. Sign out and back in if the section does not appear immediately.

Read the complete installation guide

docs.title: Start safely
docs.text:
UmbraScript can make broad changes quickly. Begin with a read-only command such as show content, show media, or show property, and use the same target or selection to inspect the affected items before running a command that changes data.

UmbraScript 1.0 does not provide a dry-run mode or a transaction across an entire batch. Check every per-item outcome and take an appropriate backup before making large production changes.

Run the five-minute first-command tutorial

docs.title: Requirements and current scope
docs.text:
• Umbraco CMS 17 or later
  • One statement per execution
  • Content, property, and media commands
  • JSON results

UmbraScript 1.0 does not currently define variables, comments, control flow, or multi-statement scripts. Property commands operate on content rather than media, and property changes save content without publishing it.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• Documentation
  • Language guide

  • Permissions and safe use
  • Compatibility and limitations

UmbraScript is created by Ben Szymanski. If it saves you time, you can support its development.

docs.title: Administration
docs.text:
Use these pages when enabling UmbraScript for a team or operating it on an established website.

  • Permissions and safe use
  • Compatibility and limitations
  • Troubleshooting

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: UmbraScript 1.0 is designed for Umbraco CMS 17 and later.

docs.title: Language scope
docs.text:
UmbraScript 1.0 supports:

  • One statement per execution
  • Case-insensitive keywords
  • Quoted string values
  • Content, property, and media commands
  • Single-item references by key or path
  • Child and descendant selections for supported commands
  • JSON results

It does not currently define variables, comments, control flow, or multi-statement scripts.

docs.title: Property limitations
docs.text:
• Property commands currently operate on content, not media.
  • New property values are supplied as strings.
  • Set and clear commands do not select a culture or segment.
  • Property changes save content but do not publish it.

Test changes on representative content, especially when a Document Type varies by culture or uses a complex property editor.

docs.title: Tree and path behavior
docs.text:
• Content paths are Umbraco routes resolved using the default culture.
  • Media paths follow media item names and must be unambiguous at each level.
  • Keys are more stable than paths when an item may be renamed or moved.
  • The media root is a destination, not an item that can be selected with /.

docs.title: Batch behavior
docs.text:
Only commands that accept a selection can target children or descendants. Rename, move, copy, restore, and create commands target or create one item at a time.

Batch operations are not documented as transactional. Always inspect per-item outcomes.

docs.title: Permissions and safe use
docs.text: UmbraScript can make broad changes quickly. Limit access, preview selections, and treat result checking as part of every operation.

docs.title: Grant access deliberately
docs.text:
Access to the UmbraScript backoffice section is assigned through Umbraco user groups. Grant it only to people who are trusted to inspect and change the same content and media through the backoffice.

Mutation commands require a signed-in backoffice user. UmbraScript supplies that user's identity to Umbraco when it saves or performs editing operations.

docs.title: Preview before changing data
docs.text:
Use show content, show media, or show property with the exact selection you plan to change.

UmbraScript
show content below "/news/2025/"

Only continue after checking every selected item.

docs.title: Prefer the smallest scope
docs.text:
• Use a key or at for one item.
  • Use in for direct children.
  • Use below only when every depth is intended.

Remember that in and below exclude their anchor item.

docs.title: Understand immediate effects
docs.text:
These commands modify data:

  • create, rename, move, and copy
  • publish and unpublish
  • set property and clear property
  • trash and restore

UmbraScript 1.0 does not provide a dry-run mode or transaction across an entire batch. Take an appropriate backup before a large production change.

docs.title: Check every result
docs.text:
Do not rely only on a summary string. For batch-capable commands, compare attempted, succeeded, and failed, then inspect each item result.

Keep the output when you need an audit record of the requested change and its outcome.

docs.title: The UmbraScript section is missing
docs.text:
1. Confirm that the package is referenced by the Umbraco project.
  2. Rebuild and restart the website.
  3. Confirm that the user's group has access to the UmbraScript section under Users and User Groups.
  4. Sign out and back in after changing group access.

docs.title: A path does not resolve
docs.text:
For content:

  • Begin the route with /.
  • Use at for a single-item path reference.
  • Confirm the route in the website's default culture.

For media:

  • Follow media item names from the media root.
  • Ensure each path segment has a unique matching sibling.
  • Use the media key if a name is ambiguous.

See References and selections.

docs.title: A key is rejected
docs.text:
A bare quoted reference must be a GUID:

UmbraScript
show content "b01b9237-ca8d-499a-aa97-de894cab5e3b"

A path without at is interpreted as a key and produces US3001.

docs.title: A command selected too many items
docs.text: Rename, move, copy, trash, and restore commands operate on one item. Use a key or at "<path>", not in or below.

docs.title: A property update failed
docs.text:
Check the per-item result:

  • propertyExists indicates whether the content type contains the alias.
  • oldValue and newValue show the attempted change.
  • outcome contains the Umbraco operation result.

Confirm that the property editor accepts a string in the supplied format. Variant properties require additional care because UmbraScript 1.0 does not select a culture or segment.

docs.title: A batch only partially succeeded
docs.text: Compare attempted, succeeded, and failed, then inspect every per-item outcome. Do not assume that successful earlier changes were rolled back. Resolve the individual failures and retry only the items that still require the operation.

docs.title: Get started
docs.text: Install UmbraScript, enable the backoffice section for your user group, and run a read-only command against your content tree.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
You need:

  • An Umbraco CMS 17 or later website
  • Access to the project that contains the Umbraco .csproj file
  • Permission to restart the website
  • An Umbraco backoffice account

docs.title: Your path to a first result
docs.text:
1. Install and enable UmbraScript.
  2. Run your first command.
  3. Learn how references and selections identify items in a tree.
  4. Use the command reference when you are ready to do more.

Warning

Several UmbraScript commands change content or media immediately. Read Permissions and safe use before running a batch or destructive command on a production site.

docs.title: Run your first command
docs.text: Use show content to read one item from the content tree. This tutorial does not modify the item.

docs.title: Choose a content item
docs.text:
Find a content item with a route you know. This tutorial uses:

/destinations/pensacola-florida/

Content paths begin with / and are written inside double quotation marks.

docs.title: Run the command
docs.text:
Open the UmbraScript console, enter the following statement, and run it:

UmbraScript
show content at "/destinations/pensacola-florida/"

Replace the example path if it does not exist on your website.

docs.title: Read the result
docs.text:
A successful result contains one content summary:

{
  "content": [
    {
      "key": "b01b9237-ca8d-499a-aa97-de894cab5e3b",
      "id": 1138,
      "name": "Pensacola, Florida",
      "contentTypeAlias": "destination",
      "created": "2026-07-07T07:13:44.29618Z",
      "lastModified": "2026-08-05T08:51:24.248402Z"
    }
  ]
}

The fields identify the item and its Document Type. Keep the key when you need a stable reference that does not depend on the item's route.

docs.title: Explore the children
docs.text:
Change at to in and use a parent path:

UmbraScript
show content in "/destinations/"

in selects the direct children of the referenced item. It does not include the parent itself.

You now know how to run a statement, reference an item by path, and inspect a selection. Continue with References and selections, or browse the content command reference.

docs.title: Install and enable UmbraScript
docs.text: Add the UmbraScript package to an Umbraco CMS project, restart the website, and grant the appropriate user groups access to its backoffice section.

docs.title: Install the package
docs.text:
Open a terminal in the directory that contains your Umbraco .csproj file, then run:

dotnet add package UmbraScript

Build and restart the website so Umbraco can discover the package:

dotnet build
dotnet run

If your website is managed by another hosting process, use that process to rebuild and restart it instead.

docs.title: Grant section access
docs.text:
An administrator must grant access to the UmbraScript section through an Umbraco user group.

  1. Sign in to the Umbraco backoffice as an administrator.
  2. Open Users.
  3. Open User Groups and select the group that should use UmbraScript.
  4. Under Assign access, enable the UmbraScript section.
  5. Save the user group.
  6. Sign out and back in if the new section does not appear immediately.

Grant access only to people who understand the effect of the commands they will run. Read Permissions and safe use before enabling a production user group.

docs.title: Verify the installation
docs.text:
Open the UmbraScript section in the backoffice. The console should be available for the signed-in user.

Continue with Run your first command.

docs.title: Update UmbraScript
docs.text:
To install a specific package version, pass the version to the .NET CLI:

dotnet add package UmbraScript --version <VERSION>

Rebuild and restart the website after changing the package version.

docs.title: How-to guides
docs.text:
Use these guides when you already know the basics and want to complete a specific task.

  • Inspect a content or media tree
  • Publish content in batches
  • Update property values safely
  • Organize media

For exact grammar and result fields, use the command reference.

docs.title: Publish content in batches
docs.text: Publish direct children or every descendant of a content item, then check the per-item outcome.

docs.title: Preview the selection
docs.text:
Run show content first:

UmbraScript
show content below "/news/2025/"

Confirm that the list contains every item you intend to publish and no others. below includes all depths but excludes the /news/2025/ anchor.

docs.title: Publish the selection
docs.text:
Use the same selection with publish content:

UmbraScript
publish content below "/news/2025/"

Use in instead when you want only direct children:

UmbraScript
publish content in "/news/2025/"

docs.title: Check the result
docs.text:
Verify that:

  • attempted matches the previewed item count.
  • failed is 0.
  • Every item in content has success set to true.

If an item fails, read its outcome before retrying. A successful item is not automatically rolled back because another item failed.

To reverse the operation, preview the same selection again and use unpublish content.

docs.title: Inspect a tree
docs.text: Use show content or show media to find a key, check a path, or preview a selection before another command.

docs.title: Inspect one item
docs.text:
Reference the item by path:

UmbraScript
show content at "/destinations/chicago/"

Copy the returned key when later commands should keep targeting the same item even if its route changes.

docs.title: List direct children
docs.text:
Use in to inspect one level below the anchor:

UmbraScript
show content in "/destinations/"

For media, paths follow media item names:

UmbraScript
show media in "/Images/Destinations/"

docs.title: List every descendant
docs.text:
Use below to include descendants at every depth:

UmbraScript
show content below "/news/2025/"

Large trees can return large results. Start with in when you do not yet know the branch structure.

docs.title: Use the selection in another command
docs.text:
After verifying every returned item, reuse the portion after content or media:

UmbraScript
publish content below "/news/2025/"

The selection reference describes all supported key and path forms.

docs.title: Organize media
docs.text: Create a destination folder, inspect the source item, then move or copy it.

docs.title: Create a folder
docs.text:
Create an Archive folder below Images:

UmbraScript
create media folder named "Archive" at "/Images/"

docs.title: Inspect the source
docs.text:
Check that the path identifies one item:

UmbraScript
show media at "/Images/legacy-logo.png"

If sibling items share a name and the path is ambiguous, use the returned media key in later commands.

docs.title: Move or copy the item
docs.text:
Move the original:

UmbraScript
move media at "/Images/legacy-logo.png" to at "/Images/Archive/"

Or create a copy with a new name:

UmbraScript
copy media at "/Images/legacy-logo.png" to at "/Images/Archive/" with name "Legacy logo archive"

Copying media duplicates its stored file and property values. Check the result before removing the source.

docs.title: Verify the destination
docs.text:
UmbraScript
show media in "/Images/Archive/"

Review the returned key, name, media type, dimensions, and file type.

docs.title: Update property values safely
docs.text: Inspect a property's current values, make the change, and review every item result.

docs.title: Inspect the current values
docs.text:
Use the property alias and the intended selection:

UmbraScript
show property "region" of content in "/destinations/"

The result tells you whether each content type contains the property and whether it currently has a value.

docs.title: Set the value
docs.text:
After checking the selection, run:

UmbraScript
set property "region" of content in "/destinations/" to "Midwest"

Property values are supplied as strings. Confirm that the property's editor accepts the value format.

docs.title: Check the result
docs.text:
Review attempted, succeeded, and failed. Each content result includes propertyExists, oldValue, newValue, success, and outcome.

Setting a property saves the content item; it does not publish it. Publish separately when that is your intended workflow.

docs.title: Clear a value
docs.text:
Preview again, then use clear property:

UmbraScript
clear property "legacyCode" of content below "/destinations/"

Warning

clear property removes the stored value from every selected item that has the property. UmbraScript 1.0 does not select a culture or segment, so test set and clear operations carefully on variant content.

docs.title: Language guide
docs.text:
UmbraScript statements read like short instructions. Each statement combines an action, a resource, and the information needed to identify or change that resource.

UmbraScript
publish content below "/news/"

In this example:

  • publish is the action.
  • content is the resource.
  • below "/news/" selects every descendant of the News item.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text:
• Mental model explains how actions, resources, and tree targets fit together.
  • Statements and keywords explains word order, whitespace, and case sensitivity.
  • Strings explains quoted values and escape sequences.
  • References and selections explains keys, paths, at, in, and below.
  • Destinations explains root and parent destinations for create, move, and copy commands.
  • Results and errors explains JSON results and diagnostic codes.

Use the command reference for the exact grammar and behavior of each statement.

docs.title: Destinations
docs.text: Create, move, and copy commands place an item under a destination parent or at the root of a tree.

docs.title: Move and copy destinations
docs.text:
Use one of these forms after to:

Form Destination to root The content or media root to "<key>" The item identified by a key to at "<path>" The item identified by a path UmbraScript
move content at "/news/old-story/" to at "/archive/"

The repeated prepositions are intentional: to introduces the destination, and at introduces a path reference.

UmbraScript
copy media at "/Images/logo.png" to root with name "Logo copy"

Content destinations are content nodes. Media destinations should normally be media folders.

docs.title: Create destinations
docs.text:
Create commands include at as part of their grammar. The forms are:

Form Destination at root The tree root at "<key>" The item identified by a key at "<path>" The item identified by a path UmbraScript
create content named "Release notes" of type "article" at "/news/"
UmbraScript
create media folder named "Archive" at root

Create commands do not use at at before a path.

docs.title: Mental model
docs.text:
UmbraScript is a small, task-focused language that maps readable statements onto Umbraco CMS operations.

It is inspired by the approachable command style of HyperTalk, AppleScript, and Hyperscript, but its vocabulary and data model are designed around Umbraco.

docs.title: Action, resource, and target
docs.text:
Most statements have three parts:

UmbraScript
show content below "/destinations/"
  • show describes the action.
  • content describes the resource.
  • below "/destinations/" describes the target selection.

Commands that change a value or location add another clause:

UmbraScript
rename content at "/news/old-title/" to "New title"

UmbraScript is readable, but it is not free-form natural language. The parser accepts a defined vocabulary and word order so that each statement has one predictable meaning.

docs.title: Trees are the organizing model
docs.text:
Content and media are addressed as trees. A statement can target:

  • One item by key or path
  • The direct children of an item
  • Every descendant of an item
  • A root or parent destination

The same selection concepts are reused by read commands and batch-capable mutation commands. This lets you preview with show before applying a change.

docs.title: Umbraco remains the source of truth
docs.text:
UmbraScript does not create a second content model. Document Type aliases, property aliases, routes, keys, culture behavior, editing operations, and operation outcomes come from Umbraco CMS.

The language translates a statement into an Umbraco operation and returns structured JSON describing what was read or attempted.

docs.title: Small language, explicit effects
docs.text:
UmbraScript 1.0 intentionally focuses on one statement at a time. There are no variables, loops, or hidden multi-step workflows. Batch behavior comes from explicit tree selections such as in and below.

Continue with Statements and keywords for the lexical rules or References and selections for the tree grammar.

docs.title: References and selections
docs.text: References identify one content or media item. Selections use a reference as an anchor and choose the anchor, its direct children, or all its descendants.

docs.title: Reference one item
docs.text:
Use a key when you need a stable identity:

UmbraScript
show content "b01b9237-ca8d-499a-aa97-de894cab5e3b"

Use at before a path when you reference one item:

UmbraScript
show content at "/destinations/pensacola-florida/"
Form Selects "<key>" The item with the specified GUID key at "<path>" The item at the specified path

docs.title: Select children or descendants
docs.text:
Use in for direct children:

UmbraScript
show content in "/destinations/"

Use below for all descendants at every depth:

UmbraScript
show content below "/destinations/"

The anchor item is not included in an in or below selection.

Scope Path form Key form Selects Self at "/path/" "<key>" The referenced item Children in "/path/" in "<key>" Direct children Descendants below "/path/" below "<key>" Descendants at every depth

Notice that at belongs to a single-item path reference. Do not write in at or below at.

docs.title: Content paths
docs.text:
A content path is an absolute Umbraco route and must begin with /. UmbraScript resolves the route using the website's default culture. It checks draft routes as well as published routes.

Routes can change when content is renamed or moved. Use a key when a command must continue to target the same item after structural changes.

docs.title: Media paths
docs.text:
A media path begins with / and follows media item names from the media root:

UmbraScript
show media at "/Images/Destinations/Chicago hero.jpg"

Media path matching is case-insensitive. Each segment must identify exactly one item among its siblings. If siblings have the same name, the path is ambiguous; use the media key instead.

The path / represents the media root, not a media item. Use a root destination when a create, move, or copy command should target the media root.

docs.title: Preview a selection
docs.text:
Before a command that changes several items, run the corresponding show command with the same selection:

UmbraScript
show content below "/news/2025/"

Check every returned item before replacing show with publish, unpublish, set, or clear.

docs.title: Results and errors
docs.text: UmbraScript returns structured JSON. Read commands return the selected data. Commands that change data report the attempted operation and its outcome.

docs.title: Read results
docs.text:
show content and show media return arrays. An at or key reference normally returns an array with one item; in and below can return several.

{
  "content": [
    {
      "key": "b01b9237-ca8d-499a-aa97-de894cab5e3b",
      "id": 1138,
      "name": "Pensacola, Florida",
      "contentTypeAlias": "destination"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Mutation results
docs.text:
Batch-capable commands commonly include:

Field Meaning summary or requestedStatus The requested operation attempted Number of selected items processed succeeded Number of successful item operations failed Number of unsuccessful item operations content or results Per-item details

Single-item commands include an item key and name plus fields such as success, result, outcome, or message.

Warning

Do not treat a returned batch as transactional. Check failed and every per-item outcome. UmbraScript does not promise that earlier successful changes will be rolled back when another item fails.

docs.title: Language diagnostics
docs.text:
Language errors include a code and the line and column at which parsing failed.

Code Meaning US1001 Unexpected character US1002 Unterminated string US1003 Invalid escape sequence US1004 Unknown word US2001 Expected a different token US2002 Unexpected token US2003 Expected a recognized statement US3001 Invalid GUID key US3002 The resource does not support the action US3003 Unsupported reference US3004 Expected content or media

Runtime errors describe failures such as an item not being found, an ambiguous media path, a missing Document Type, or a command resolving more items than it supports. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Statements and keywords
docs.text:
UmbraScript 1.0 accepts one statement per execution. A statement must use the expected words in the expected order.

UmbraScript
rename content at "/news/old-title/" to "New title"

docs.title: One statement at a time
docs.text:
The parser expects the statement to end after the command is complete. A second statement or unexplained text produces an error.

show content at "/news/" publish content at "/news/"

Run these as two separate submissions instead.

docs.title: Keywords are case-insensitive
docs.text:
The following statements have the same meaning:

UmbraScript
show media in "/Images/"
UmbraScript
SHOW MEDIA IN "/Images/"

Lowercase keywords are used throughout this documentation for consistency.

docs.title: Whitespace is flexible
docs.text:
Spaces, tabs, and line breaks separate tokens. They do not change the meaning of a valid statement.

UmbraScript
create content
named "Release notes"
of type "article"
at "/news/"

docs.title: Reserved words
docs.text:
UmbraScript 1.0 recognizes these words:

Actions Resources and grammar show, publish, unpublish, trash, restore, rename, clear, move, copy, create, set content, media, folder, property, properties, name, named, at, below, in, with, type, of, to, root

Names, aliases, paths, keys, and values are not keywords. Write them as quoted strings.

docs.title: Comments and variables
docs.text: UmbraScript 1.0 does not define comments, variables, or multi-statement scripts. Characters or words outside the supported grammar produce a diagnostic.

docs.title: Strings
docs.text:
Write keys, paths, names, aliases, and property values inside double quotation marks.

UmbraScript
set property "pageTitle" of content at "/news/" to "Today's news"

docs.title: Escape sequences
docs.text:
Use a backslash when a string must contain a quotation mark, backslash, or control character.

Sequence Value \" Double quotation mark \\ Backslash \n Line feed \r Carriage return \t Tab

For example:

UmbraScript
rename content at "/news/todays-news/" to "Today's \"Top Story\""

An unsupported escape sequence produces diagnostic US1003. A missing closing quotation mark produces US1002.

docs.title: Property values
docs.text:
Property commands accept the new value as a string, even when the property represents a number or another data type.

UmbraScript
set property "latitude" of content at "/destinations/chicago/" to "41.8781"

The Umbraco property editor determines how the value is stored. Test property updates on representative content before applying them to a selection.

docs.title: Command reference
docs.text: The reference describes the exact syntax, supported scope, behavior, result fields, and common failures for every UmbraScript 1.0 command.

docs.title: Command groups
docs.text:
• Content commands inspect and manage the content tree.
  • Property commands read and change content property values.
  • Media commands inspect and organize the media tree.

docs.title: Syntax notation
docs.text:
Reference pages use placeholders inside angle brackets:

Placeholder Meaning <key> A GUID key written as a quoted string <path> An absolute path written as a quoted string <reference> One item identified by "<key>" or at "<path>" <selection> A reference, in "<key-or-path>", or below "<key-or-path>" <destination> root, "<key>", or at "<path>"

Square brackets indicate an optional clause. Do not type the angle or square brackets when running a command.

Read References and selections and Destinations for the complete forms.

docs.title: Results
docs.text: Result property names are shown in their JSON form. See Results and errors for common batch fields and diagnostic codes.

docs.title: Content commands
docs.text:
Content commands inspect and manage nodes in the Umbraco content tree.

Command Scope Changes data show content Item, children, or descendants No create content One destination Yes publish content Item, children, or descendants Yes unpublish content Item, children, or descendants Yes rename content One item Yes move content One item Yes copy content One item Yes trash content One item Yes restore content One item Yes

Use property commands to inspect or change content property values.

Tip

Run show content with the intended reference or selection before a command that changes data.

docs.title: Copy content
docs.text: Copies one content item under another content item or to the content root. The copied item can be given a new name.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: copy content <reference> to <destination> [with name "<new-name>"]

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Copy and rename an item:

UmbraScript
copy content at "/news/story/" to at "/archive/" with name "Story archive"

Copy an item to the root without renaming it:

UmbraScript
copy content "b01b9237-ca8d-499a-aa97-de894cab5e3b" to root

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text: The copy does not include descendants and is not related to the original through an Umbraco relation. When with name is present, UmbraScript copies first and then attempts a separate rename save.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The result contains batch summary counts and a one-item content array. The item distinguishes copySucceeded from the optional renameSucceeded and includes the source, destination, copied key, and final name.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Requires access to the UmbraScript section and a signed-in backoffice user for the copy and optional rename operations.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text:
• The source or destination cannot be resolved.
  • The source resolves to more than one item.
  • The requested name is empty.
  • The copy succeeds but the requested rename fails; inspect both result fields.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Destinations
  • Move content

docs.title: Create content
docs.text: Creates one content item with the specified name and Document Type alias under a parent or at the content root.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
create content named "<name>" of type "<document-type-alias>" at root
create content named "<name>" of type "<document-type-alias>" at "<parent-key>"
create content named "<name>" of type "<document-type-alias>" at "<parent-path>"

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Create an item below News:

UmbraScript
create content named "Release notes" of type "article" at "/news/"

Create an item at the content root:

UmbraScript
create content named "Site notice" of type "notice" at root

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text: The new item has no initial property values. For a Document Type that varies by culture, UmbraScript uses the website's default culture for the initial name. The command creates but does not publish the item.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The result contains summary, key, name, docType, success, and result. key is null when creation fails.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Requires access to the UmbraScript section and a signed-in backoffice user for the create operation.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text:
• The name is empty or whitespace.
  • The Document Type alias does not exist.
  • The parent key or path cannot be resolved.
  • Umbraco rejects the parent, Document Type, culture, or current user's operation.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Destinations
  • Set a property
  • Publish content

docs.title: Move content
docs.text:
Moves one content item under another content item or to the content root.

Warning

Moving content changes its place in the tree and can change its route. Use the key when later operations must target the moved item reliably.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: move content <reference> to <destination>

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Move an item under Archive:

UmbraScript
move content at "/news/old-story/" to at "/archive/"

Move an item to the content root:

UmbraScript
move content "b01b9237-ca8d-499a-aa97-de894cab5e3b" to root

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The result contains summary, attempted, succeeded, failed, and a one-item content array. The item records the source, destination, success, and Umbraco result.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Requires access to the UmbraScript section and a signed-in backoffice user for the move operation.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text:
• The source or destination cannot be resolved.
  • The source resolves to more than one item.
  • The destination is not valid for the source Document Type.
  • Umbraco rejects the move for the current user or tree state.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Destinations
  • Copy content

docs.title: Publish content
docs.text:
Publishes one content item, the direct children of an item, or every descendant of an item.

Warning

A scoped selection can publish many items immediately. Preview it with show content before running this command.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: publish content <selection>

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Publish one item by path:

UmbraScript
publish content at "/destinations/pensacola-florida/"

Publish direct children:

UmbraScript
publish content in "/destinations/"

Publish every descendant:

UmbraScript
publish content below "/destinations/"

The in and below forms do not publish the anchor item.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The result contains requestedStatus, attempted, succeeded, failed, and a content array. Each item contains key, name, success, and outcome.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Requires access to the UmbraScript section and a signed-in backoffice user for the publish operations.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text:
• The reference cannot be resolved.
  • An item is invalid for publishing.
  • Umbraco rejects the operation for the current user or content state.

Check every item outcome. A failed item does not roll back items that were already published.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Publish content in batches
  • Unpublish content

docs.title: Rename content
docs.text: Changes the name of one content item and saves it.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: rename content <reference> to "<new-name>"

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Rename by path:

UmbraScript
rename content at "/news/old-title/" to "New title"

Rename by key:

UmbraScript
rename content "b01b9237-ca8d-499a-aa97-de894cab5e3b" to "Pensacola guide"

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text: The command saves the new name but does not publish the item. A rename can change the draft route, so retain the item key when a later command must target the same item.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The result contains key, oldName, newName, success, and message.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Requires access to the UmbraScript section and a signed-in backoffice user for the save operation.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text:
• The reference does not resolve to exactly one content item.
  • The new name is not accepted by Umbraco.
  • The current user is unavailable for the save operation.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Publish content
  • References and selections

docs.title: Restore content
docs.text: Restores one content item from the Umbraco recycle bin.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: restore content <reference>

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Use a key because a recycled item's former route may no longer resolve:

UmbraScript
restore content "b01b9237-ca8d-499a-aa97-de894cab5e3b"

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The result contains key, name, success, and result.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Requires access to the UmbraScript section and a signed-in backoffice user for the restore operation.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text:
• The key cannot be found.
  • The reference does not resolve to exactly one item.
  • Umbraco cannot determine or use a restore destination.
  • The current user cannot perform the restore operation.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Trash content
  • Show content

docs.title: Show content
docs.text: Returns summary information for one content item or a selection from the content tree. This command does not modify content.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
show content <selection>

<selection> supports a key, at path, in selection, or below selection.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Show one item by key:

UmbraScript
show content "b01b9237-ca8d-499a-aa97-de894cab5e3b"

Show one item by route:

UmbraScript
show content at "/destinations/pensacola-florida/"

Show every descendant of a branch:

UmbraScript
show content below "/destinations/"

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The content array contains key, id, name, contentTypeAlias, created, and lastModified for every selected item.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text:
• A bare quoted value is not a valid GUID.
  • A content route cannot be found in the default culture.
  • Umbraco cannot load a child or descendant returned by the navigation service.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• References and selections
  • Show all properties

docs.title: Trash content
docs.text:
Moves one content item to the Umbraco recycle bin.

Warning

Confirm the item with show content before moving it to the recycle bin.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: trash content <reference>

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
UmbraScript
trash content at "/news/old-story/"

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The result contains key, name, success, and result.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Requires access to the UmbraScript section and a signed-in backoffice user for the recycle-bin operation.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text:
• The reference cannot be resolved.
  • The command does not resolve to exactly one item.
  • Umbraco rejects the recycle-bin operation for the current user or content state.

Keep the returned key if you may need to restore the item.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Restore content
  • Permissions and safe use

docs.title: Unpublish content
docs.text:
Unpublishes one content item, the direct children of an item, or every descendant of an item.

Warning

Unpublishing can remove pages from the public website immediately. Preview a scoped selection with show content first.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: unpublish content <selection>

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Unpublish one item by path:

UmbraScript
unpublish content at "/destinations/pensacola-florida/"

Unpublish direct children:

UmbraScript
unpublish content in "/destinations/"

Unpublish every descendant:

UmbraScript
unpublish content below "/destinations/"

For a descendant selection, UmbraScript processes the resolved items in reverse order so deeper items are handled before earlier ancestors in the result set.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The result contains requestedStatus, attempted, succeeded, failed, and a content array. Each item contains key, name, success, and outcome.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Requires access to the UmbraScript section and a signed-in backoffice user for the unpublish operations.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text:
• The reference cannot be resolved.
  • An item is already in an incompatible state.
  • Umbraco rejects the operation for the current user or content state.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Publish content
  • References and selections

docs.title: Media commands
docs.text:
Media commands inspect and organize items in the Umbraco media tree.

Command Scope Changes data show media Item, children, or descendants No create media folder One destination Yes rename media One item Yes move media One item Yes copy media One item Yes trash media One item Yes restore media One item Yes

Media paths follow item names from the media root. Each path segment must have one case-insensitive match among its siblings. Use a key when names are ambiguous.

UmbraScript 1.0 creates media folders but does not upload new media files.

docs.title: Copy media
docs.text:
Copies one media item under another media item or to the media root. The copy can be given a new name.

Note

Copying file-based media duplicates the underlying media file as well as the stored property values.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: copy media <reference> to <destination> [with name "<new-name>"]

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Copy and rename an item:

UmbraScript
copy media at "/Images/legacy-logo.png" to at "/Images/Archive/" with name "Legacy logo archive"

Copy an item to the root:

UmbraScript
copy media "b01b9237-ca8d-499a-aa97-de894cab5e3b" to root

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text: UmbraScript creates a new media item of the same media type, copies culture names and property values, and duplicates files recognized by Umbraco's media URL generators. When with name is present, the copy and rename are reported separately.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The result contains summary, attempted, succeeded, failed, and a one-item results array. The item distinguishes copySucceeded from renameSucceeded and includes the source, destination, copied key, and final name.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Requires access to the UmbraScript section and a signed-in backoffice user for the copy and optional rename operations.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text:
• The source or destination cannot be resolved unambiguously.
  • The requested name is empty.
  • A referenced source file cannot be copied.
  • A property editor exposes a file reference in an unsupported form.
  • The copy succeeds but the optional rename fails.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Organize media
  • Move media

docs.title: Create a media folder
docs.text: Creates one folder under another media item or at the media root.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
create media folder named "<name>" at root
create media folder named "<name>" at "<parent-key>"
create media folder named "<name>" at "<parent-path>"

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Create a folder below Images:

UmbraScript
create media folder named "Archive" at "/Images/"

Create a root folder:

UmbraScript
create media folder named "Imports" at root

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The result contains summary, key, name, success, and result. key is null when creation fails.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Requires access to the UmbraScript section and a signed-in backoffice user for the create operation.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text:
• The folder name is empty or whitespace.
  • The parent key or path cannot be resolved.
  • The media path is ambiguous.
  • Umbraco rejects the parent or the current user's operation.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Destinations
  • Organize media

docs.title: Move media
docs.text:
Moves one media item under another media item or to the media root.

Warning

Moving an item changes its media path. Use its key when later operations must target it reliably.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: move media <reference> to <destination>

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Move an item into Archive:

UmbraScript
move media at "/Images/legacy-logo.png" to at "/Images/Archive/"

Move an item to the media root:

UmbraScript
move media "b01b9237-ca8d-499a-aa97-de894cab5e3b" to root

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The result contains summary, attempted, succeeded, failed, and a one-item content array. The item records the source, destination, success, and Umbraco result.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Requires access to the UmbraScript section and a signed-in backoffice user for the move operation.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text:
• The source or destination cannot be resolved.
  • A source or destination path is ambiguous.
  • The destination is not valid for the media item.
  • Umbraco rejects the move for the current user or tree state.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Destinations
  • Copy media

docs.title: Rename media
docs.text: Changes the name of one media item and saves it.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: rename media <reference> to "<new-name>"

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Rename by path:

UmbraScript
rename media at "/Images/old-logo.png" to "Primary logo"

Rename by key:

UmbraScript
rename media "b01b9237-ca8d-499a-aa97-de894cab5e3b" to "Primary logo"

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text: Renaming an item changes the name segment used by UmbraScript media paths. Retain the item key when a later command must target the renamed item.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The result contains key, oldName, newName, success, and message.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Requires access to the UmbraScript section and a signed-in backoffice user for the save operation.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text:
• The reference does not resolve to exactly one media item.
  • The path is ambiguous.
  • Umbraco rejects the name or save operation.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Media paths
  • Move media

docs.title: Restore media
docs.text: Restores one media item from the Umbraco recycle bin.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: restore media <reference>

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Use a key because a recycled item's former media path may no longer resolve:

UmbraScript
restore media "b01b9237-ca8d-499a-aa97-de894cab5e3b"

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The result contains key, name, success, and result.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Requires access to the UmbraScript section and a signed-in backoffice user for the restore operation.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text:
• The key cannot be found.
  • The reference does not resolve to exactly one media item.
  • Umbraco cannot determine or use a restore destination.
  • The current user cannot perform the restore operation.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Trash media
  • Show media

docs.title: Show media
docs.text: Returns summary information for one media item or a selection from the media tree. This command does not modify media.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: show media <selection>

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Show one item by key:

UmbraScript
show media "b01b9237-ca8d-499a-aa97-de894cab5e3b"

Show one item by media path:

UmbraScript
show media at "/Images/Destinations/Chicago hero.jpg"

Show direct children of a folder:

UmbraScript
show media in "/Images/Destinations/"

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The content array contains key, id, name, contentTypeAlias, created, lastModified, width, height, and fileType. Dimension and file-type fields can be null when the media type does not supply them.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text:
• A bare quoted value is not a valid GUID.
  • A media path segment does not exist.
  • A media path is ambiguous because siblings share a name.
  • The path / is used as an item reference.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Media paths
  • Organize media

docs.title: Trash media
docs.text:
Moves one media item to the Umbraco recycle bin.

Warning

Confirm the item with show media before moving it to the recycle bin.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: trash media <reference>

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
UmbraScript
trash media at "/Images/unused-banner.jpg"

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The result contains key, name, success, and result.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Requires access to the UmbraScript section and a signed-in backoffice user for the recycle-bin operation.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text:
• The reference does not resolve to exactly one media item.
  • The media path is ambiguous.
  • Umbraco rejects the recycle-bin operation.

Keep the returned key if you may need to restore the item.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Restore media
  • Permissions and safe use

docs.title: Property commands
docs.text:
Property commands inspect or change property values on content items.

Command Scope Changes data show property Item, children, or descendants No show properties Item, children, or descendants No set property Item, children, or descendants Yes clear property Item, children, or descendants Yes

Property commands use the property's alias, not its display name. UmbraScript 1.0 property commands operate on content only.

Warning

Set and clear commands save content but do not publish it. They do not select a culture or segment, so test changes carefully on variant content.

docs.title: Clear a property
docs.text:
Removes one stored property value and saves every selected content item.

Warning

Preview the same property and selection with show property. Clearing a scoped selection can remove values from many items.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: clear property "<property-alias>" of content <selection>

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Clear one value:

UmbraScript
clear property "legacyCode" of content at "/destinations/chicago/"

Clear values from every descendant:

UmbraScript
clear property "legacyCode" of content below "/destinations/"

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text: UmbraScript removes the value and saves each item but does not publish it. The command does not select a culture or segment.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
The result contains summary, attempted, succeeded, failed, and a content array. Each item includes propertyExists, oldValue, a null newValue, success, and outcome.

If a content type does not contain the alias, that item is returned as a failure with propertyExists set to false.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Requires access to the UmbraScript section and a signed-in backoffice user for each content save.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text:
• The content reference cannot be resolved.
  • The selected content does not contain the property.
  • Umbraco rejects the save operation.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Show a property
  • Set a property
  • Permissions and safe use

docs.title: Set a property
docs.text:
Sets one property value and saves every selected content item.

Warning

Preview the same property and selection with show property before running this command. A scoped selection can update many items.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: set property "<property-alias>" of content <selection> to "<new-value>"

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Set one value:

UmbraScript
set property "latitude" of content at "/destinations/chicago/" to "41.8781"

Set the same value on direct children:

UmbraScript
set property "region" of content in "/destinations/" to "Midwest"

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text: The new value is supplied as a string. UmbraScript saves each item but does not publish it. The command does not select a culture or segment.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
The result contains summary, attempted, succeeded, failed, and a content array. Each item includes propertyExists, oldValue, newValue, success, and outcome.

If a content type does not contain the alias, that item is returned as a failure with propertyExists set to false.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Requires access to the UmbraScript section and a signed-in backoffice user for each content save.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text:
• The content reference cannot be resolved.
  • The property editor does not accept the supplied string format.
  • Umbraco rejects the save operation.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Update property values safely
  • Clear a property
  • Publish content

docs.title: Show all properties
docs.text: Returns every property and current value for each selected content item. This command does not modify content.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: show properties of content <selection>

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Show every property on one item:

UmbraScript
show properties of content at "/destinations/chicago/"

Show every property on direct children:

UmbraScript
show properties of content in "/destinations/"

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
The result contains summary, count, and a content array. Each content entry includes key, id, name, contentTypeAlias, and a properties object keyed by property alias.

The returned values are the stored property values. Their JSON shapes depend on the Umbraco property editors in use.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text:
• The content reference cannot be resolved.
  • The selection's children or descendants cannot be loaded.
  • The statement names a resource other than content.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Show a property
  • Update property values safely

docs.title: Show a property
docs.text: Returns one property value for every selected content item. This command does not modify content.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: show property "<property-alias>" of content <selection>

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Show one value:

UmbraScript
show property "latitude" of content at "/destinations/chicago/"

Show the value for direct children:

UmbraScript
show property "region" of content in "/destinations/"

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
The properties array contains one entry per selected content item:

Field Meaning key and name The content item propertyAlias The requested alias propertyExists Whether the content type contains the property hasValue Whether the stored value is non-null value The stored value, or null

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text:
• The content reference cannot be resolved.
  • The selection's children or descendants cannot be loaded.
  • The statement names a resource other than content.

A missing property is reported in the result rather than raised as a language error.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Show all properties
  • Set a property
